pr_title: Add EVP demos for RSA-PSS signing and verification
pr_body:
Two demos are provided: one using RSA-PSS directly in which a digest must be provided, and one using RSA-PSS with the EVP_DigestSign APIs which performs the hashing for you.

Fixes #14113.
pr_comments: Updated to use EVP_MD_fetch rather than EVP_sha256.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but this PR has failing CI tests.  Once the tests pass it will get moved to 'approval: ready to merge' automatically, alternatively please review and set the label manually.

issue_context.title: Add an EVP signature demo for RSA
issue_context.body:
Use RSA OAEP.  Do both validation and signature generation.

It should be the current best practice (fetch), have proper error handling and resource allocation/deallocation and be in the style of a known answer test.
comments:
I have a rough draft for this but some questions:

* AIUI OAEP is only applicable to encryption, not signing. What do you want to use?
* PSS is non-deterministic so known answer tests don't seem applicable.
IMO it should be RSA-PSS and KAT is not really needed. Just create a signature with one function and verify it with another.

review_comments: I seem to recall it being undefined behaviour if you initialise an array with less than the number of array elements?

If you use an initializer list, C specifies that any unspecified elements are zero-initialized.

(Because of this, you'd expect `= {}` to be reasonable, but the C standard is weird about this; technically you have to specify at least one value, so `= {0}`. In practice most compilers will accept `= {}`, but e.g. MSVC in C mode won't. IIRC C2x might be set to finally allow `= {}`.)

(Plus, since this is of static storage duration, it would be zero-initialized even without the initializer list here; it's technically unnecessary, and included for exposition).

From C11:
>The initialization shall occur in initializer list order, each initializer provided for a particular subobject overriding any previously listed initializer for the same subobject; all subobjects that are not initialized explicitly shall be initialized implicitly the same as objects that have static storage duration.
Yes, but we use C89. I'm not sure this is true in that version.

From C89:

>If there are fewer initializers in a list than there are members of an aggregate, the remainder of the aggregate shall be initialized implicitly the same as objects that have static storage duration.
